---
title: "Task Timing and Preference"
subtitle: "A study companion to the paper on how temporal distance weakens the impact of task difficulty but not task appeal"
---

::: {.hero}
<p class="hero-kicker">Four studies · Bayesian analysis</p>

This site collects the analysis reports for a pilot study and three experiments on how timing, difficulty, and attractiveness shape task preference. Each report moves from the design and sample to the model, results, interpretation, and reproducibility details.

:::

## Studies

::: {.study-grid}
::: {.study-card}
<span class="study-label">Pilot study</span>

### Rating calibration

Paired Bayesian comparisons assess whether task difficulty and interest ratings differ between experimental and survey contexts.

[Open the pilot report](analysis/analysis_pilot.html){.card-link}
:::

::: {.study-card}
<span class="study-label">Experiment 1</span>

### Timing and task type

An aggregated binomial-logit model estimates task-type preferences under tomorrow and future timing conditions.

[Open the Experiment 1 report](analysis/analysis_exp1.html){.card-link}
:::

::: {.study-card}
<span class="study-label">Experiment 2</span>

### Preferred delay

A Gaussian mixed model estimates preferred delay as a function of task difficulty and attractiveness.

[Open the Experiment 2 report](analysis/analysis_exp2.html){.card-link}
:::

::: {.study-card}
<span class="study-label">Experiment 3</span>

### Task acceptance

A Bernoulli-logit mixed model estimates acceptance across delay, difficulty, and attractiveness conditions.

[Open the Experiment 3 report](analysis/analysis_exp3.html){.card-link}
:::
:::

## Reproducibility and data boundary

::: {.boundary-grid}
::: {.boundary-card}
### Reproducible reports

The notebooks record the prepared inputs, model specifications, posterior summaries, and software session information used to produce each report. Analysis code is available in the source repository.
:::

::: {.boundary-card}
### Aggregate presentation

The published reports present aggregate summaries and model results. They do not display participant-level rows. Prepared analysis data remain versioned with the research source.
:::
:::
